Step 1 (provenance, all 43 shots): independently re-extracted all 129 start/mid/end PNG artifacts directly from output/film.mp4 at their exact recorded frame_index (via ffmpeg select=eq(n,X), and -ss for two frames re-run after an interrupted batch), computed sha256 of each independent extraction and of each provided output/film-reference/shot-*.png file, and confirmed all 129 match evidence.json's recorded sha256 exactly (0 mismatches) -- this directly tests whether the known render-cache staleness bug could have affected any other shot's evidence beyond the two previously named, and finds none. Step 2 (shot-0 and shot-17 independent re-verification, as specifically requested): extracted every frame 78-86 of shot-0 and 2248-2256 of shot-17 directly from film.mp4 via ffmpeg -ss (including each shot's literal first and last encoded frame), pixel-diffed every frame against an early reference frame in the same run (full-frame and a tight crop on the disputed region), and visually inspected full-resolution crops of the mid frame, next-to-last frame and literal last frame of each. Found the shot-0 music-staff graphic and 'partitur latihan'/'tempo kelompok kami' labels fully present and unchanged through frame 85 (the shot's actual last frame), and the shot-17 red header sitting clearly clear of the notebook's ring band through frame 2255 (its actual last frame); both previously-reported single-frame artifacts are not present in this render, independently confirming the stale-cache hypothesis rather than assuming it. Step 3 (shot-22 re-verification): extracted 6 frames spanning shot-22's full 90.194-92.872s window directly from film.mp4 and visually confirmed the pushed notebook's spiral-ring row crosses Ardipal's chin/jaw for roughly the first 0.5s before clearing -- unchanged in position, duration and severity from the prior round, so this known, user-accepted non-blocking issue remains correctly flagged as 'unmet' and is not worse. Step 4 (all 43 shots, fresh scrutiny): ran ffmpeg volumedetect over every shot's exact [start,end) window directly against film.mp4 for the sound check; pulled every output/film.srt caption overlapping each shot's window for the typography/timing checks; and visually inspected a composite (start|mid|end, independently re-extracted and downscaled for review) of every one of the 43 shots plus additional full-resolution crops where anything looked irregular (e.g. shot-29's questionnaire-card prop reappearing smaller alongside a new door sign at its end, found to be an intentional visual callback rather than a continuity break, not flagged). No other shot showed a cache-era artifact, broken drawing, face/prop overlap, composition crowding, caption mismatch, pacing problem or audio anomaly.
